newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Monday in thin trading ahead of the Bank of Israel announcement on February interest rates, traders said.
After the close of trading the central bank said it was lowering its key lending rate for February by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.2 percent.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.14 pct to 101.97
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.08 pct to 101.23.
Volume was a low 101 million shekels with long CPI-linked bonds posting the highest rise.
"The bond market showed strength and the whole market rose as investors predicted a rate cut of around 0.5 percentage point," said Ari Eidelheit of Zeller Eblagon Securities.
CPI-linked bonds continue to rise sharply. Eidelheit said yields on them are expected to continue to decline from 4.3 percent to four percent.
"Yields of 4.3 percent are still attractive and I believe that the positive trend in the bond market will continue in the near future," said a trader at Israel Discount Bank.
Eidelheit said unlinked bonds also rose because it is clear that the Bank of Israel will have to continue lowering the rates.
"Yields on unlinked bonds remained stable at 14.5 percent. If the lower inflationary trend continues these bonds and the Makam will continue to attract investors," the Discount trader added.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds closed slightly higher in response to the decline of the shekel against the U.S. currency.
In the local foreign currency market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at an old-time high of 3.3060 shekels against 3.3000 shekels on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
